s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive abdominal distension with a palpable mass
salient_findings: Markedly distended abdomen with a palpable mass
Large, fluid-filled lesion on CT of the abdomen and pelvis
key_facts: 17-year-old nulliparous female
Two-year history of gradually progressive abdominal distension
Initial presentation with bloating
No pain, vaginal bleeding, or systemic symptoms
No personal or family history of cancer
BMI 20.5 kg/m2
Blood pressure 125/85 mmHg
Pulse 89/min
SpO2 95% on room air
Hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL with a microcytic profile
APTT, INR, electrolytes, urea, and creatinine were normal
Tumor markers HE4, LDH, alpha-fetoprotein, CA-125, and β-hCG within normal limits or slightly elevated

shortlist.label: Mucinous cystadenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Large, fluid-filled ovarian lesion with a unilocular appearance and no septations or solid components

shortlist.label: Serous cystadenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Ovarian origin and large size of the lesion are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Ovarian cystadenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Although tumor markers are within normal limits, the large size and ovarian origin of the lesion make this a plausible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Dermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Ovarian origin and potential for large size, although less likely given the unilocular appearance

shortlist.label: Borderline ovarian tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Ovarian origin and large size of the lesion, with a potential for borderline malignant behavior

raw.rationale: The large, fluid-filled, unilocular lesion with a thin wall and no septations or solid components is suggestive of a mucinous cystadenoma, which is a type of benign ovarian tumor that can grow to be quite large and cause abdominal distension.

rejected.label: Ovarian cystadenocarcinoma
rejected.why: The tumor markers are within normal limits or only slightly elevated, and there is no mention of solid components or septations, which are more characteristic of malignant tumors.

rejected.label: Dermoid cyst
rejected.why: Dermoid cysts are typically smaller and more complex, with solid components and a wider range of tissue types.

rejected.label: Serous cystadenoma
rejected.why: While serous cystadenomas can be large and fluid-filled, they are less common in young women and often have more complex features.

rejected.label: Borderline ovarian tumor
rejected.why: Borderline ovarian tumors often have more complex features, such as solid components or septations, and are less likely to present as a simple, large, fluid-filled lesion.
